messages.subject: Re: Clarification of Shiny Server Pro 20 concurrent users limitation
messages.subject_clean: Clarification of Shiny Server Pro 20 concurrent users limitation
messages.body_plain:
In short, yes. However, a user a user-browser, so the same user can concurrently connect to multiple apps using the same browser and it will all count as a single user. If they concurrently connect with multiple devices, each will count separately. In either case, each connection applies to the 200 connection limit.

Chris

messages.subject: Slow down due to many persistent observers
messages.subject_clean: Slow down due to many persistent observers
messages.body_plain:
Dear community and Joe,

I have a big and complex Shiny app (over 2000 lines) that does awesome things (automatically / with an interface process many GEO micro array data sets). Basically it does a bunch of processing, then provides an interactive UI for the user to modify and verify some things, then does more processing. It works, which is awesome.

The problem is that when getting user feedback on many data sets one after the other, it eventually slows down to be unusable. I have to the best of my ability traced this to the dynamic creation of buttons (required) and paired observers, that seem to persist, resulting in hundreds of observers, and I can't find a way to get rid of them.

I guess there are two solutions I can think of, but are outside of my knowledge of Shiny and outside of my googling abilities:
1) Assign some kind of consistent ID to the observers so that they over write themselves, or confine them to a list or reactive values. I tried this but I still couldn't overwrite them. Is it to do with R making copies of objects instead of passing a reference?
2) GO in and destroy the old observers. Again I tried this by assigning the observers to a list and then lapply .... destroy on that list and it didn't seem to have any effect.

Please help.

Thank you.

Djordje

Below is a minimal example:

##############################################################
##############################################################

library(shiny)
library(DT)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  ## make a toy data frame
  DF <- data.frame(A = c(1,2), B = c(3,4), row.names = c("one","two"))
  ## make a DT output for it
  output$testData <- DT::renderDataTable(DF, selection = "single")

  output$message <- renderText("This minimal example illustrates issues with persistent observers building up over time.\nEvery time you swap between the selected rows of the table, new observers are created that monitor the dynamically created action buttons.\nEach time a button observer is invalidated it will write a message to the console. The more times you swap between selected rows, the more persistent observers are created and the more console messages you get per click. I want to remove the previously created observers when changing the selected row.\n\n")

  # get the last clicked row
  selectedRow <- reactive({
    req(input$testData_row_last_clicked)
    input$testData_row_last_clicked
  })

  # tell us which row it was
  output$selectedRow <- renderText(selectedRow())

  output$lastClick <- renderUI({

    req(selectedRow())

    list(
      lastclick =  renderText(selectedRow()),
      buttons = lapply(1:DF[selectedRow(),"A"], function(X){
        actionButton(paste0("go_", selectedRow(), X), "CLICK ME")
      })
    )

Hi Jeffrey and Joe,

No plotly server is involved unless you use the plotly_POST() function to send the figure on your plotly account for hosting. That being said, some "local" (i.e., no server) plots could be considered not entirely "offline" (i.e., require an internet connection). Specifically, choropleths require "geo asset" files which are too large to bundle with the package, so your browser will download them when you view it -- https://github.com/ropensci/plotly/pull/302

Best,

-Carson

messages.body_plain:
Dear friends

I have developed a shiny R application using RStudio, which works as a user interface for some computational work.
It gets the data from the user and save it as files and then run an external executable file which reads the files and compute some parameters and writes the results in some files.
The results will be then displayed on the Shiny interface.

> >

messages.subject: Re: Slow down due to many persistent observers
messages.subject_clean: Slow down due to many persistent observers
messages.body_plain:
Hi Joe and devs,

It turns out the slow down was not only due to persistent observers, as the problem has not gone away by destroying them - my app still becomes unusably slow as more interfaces are generated (it's fine for the first one).

Another sign I found was a build up of the data table related inputs in names(input). I reproduced the issue in the following minimal example:

#####################################################################

library(shiny)
library(DT)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  ## make a toy data frame
  DF <- data.frame(A = c(1,2), B = c(3,4), row.names = c("one","two"))
  ## make a DT output for it
  output$testData <- DT::renderDataTable(DF, selection = "single")

  output$message <- renderText("This minimal example illustrates issues with persistent inputs building up over time.\nEvery time you swap between the selected rows of the table, new inputs are created for the data frames.\nThe more times you swap between selected rows, the more persistent inputs are created. Can this be related to memory usage or something else that is slowing down my apps?\n\n")

  # get the last clicked row
  selectedRow <- reactive({
    req(input$testData_row_last_clicked)
    input$testData_row_last_clicked
  })

  # tell us which row it was
  output$selectedRow <- renderText(selectedRow())

  output$lastClick <- renderUI({

    req(selectedRow())

    list(
      lastclick =  renderText(selectedRow()),
      buttons = lapply(1:DF[selectedRow(),"A"], function(X){
        actionButton(paste0("go_", selectedRow(), X), "CLICK ME")

      }),
      datas = lapply(1:DF[selectedRow(),"A"], function(X){renderDataTable(DF[selectedRow(),]) }),
      message1 = h3(renderText(paste0("length(names(input)): ", length(names(input))))),
      message2 = h3(renderText("names(input):")),
      inputnames = renderText(names(input))
    )

  })

  observer.list <- list()

  obs <- observe({

    observer.list <<- lapply(names(input)[grepl(paste0("go_", selectedRow()), names(input))], function(x) {

      print(paste0("Made observer for :", x))
      obsr <- observeEvent(
        {input[[x]]},{
          print(paste0("BUTTON ",x," WAS CLICKED"))
        }, ignoreNULL = TRUE, autoDestroy = TRUE)
     })
  })

  obss <- observeEvent(
    {selectedRow()},{

      print("clear previously made observers")
      lapply(observer.list, function(X){ X$destroy() })
    }, ignoreNULL = TRUE, autoDestroy = TRUE, priority = 1)

}

########################################################################
# User Interface
########################################################################

ui <- fluidPage(
  mainPanel(
    textOutput("message"),
    dataTableOutput("testData"),
    uiOutput("lastClick")
  )
)

shinyApp(ui, server)

#####################################################################

As you can see from this example the number of inputs keeps increasing as you dynamically render more interfaces.

In my app I render a lot of data tables like this dynamically (2-20 per data set, 1 or more times per data set, hundreds of data sets), so this number builds up very quickly.

Could there be something I am missing here that is slowing my app down as it progresses? I do also see a constant rise in memory usage that is not intuitive. Can I remove these 'old' inputs, and will it help?

Thanks a lot.

Djordje

messages.subject: Saving the results of input$map_marker_click to table accessible in R
messages.subject_clean: Saving the results of input$map_marker_click to table accessible in R
messages.body_plain:
I am trying to create a file with a table containing the ID, lat, and long of each map marker that a user clicks on in a leaflet map displayed in shiny. This should (I presume) be relatively straightforward, but it's my first foray into both leaflet and Shiny, so thanks in advance for your patience with my lack of experience.

I've created a sample dataset to show you how my code is structured thus far. I have relied heavily on code in the demo Shiny code from: http://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/observer-demo.html. As it states on this page, the observer is writing to a log file, but I'm not sure how to access the information in that log file in r.

Thank you,

Qamar

library(shiny)
library(leaflet)

Lat<-runif (100, min=-28, max=-26)
Long<-runif(100, min=152, max=153)
Global_ID<-(1:100)
data<-as.data.frame(cbind(Lat, Long, Global_ID))

## create map

map3<-leaflet(data)
map3<-addProviderTiles(map3, "Esri.WorldImagery", group = "Satellite")
map3<-addMarkers(map3,~Long,~Lat,popup = ~as.character(Global_ID), layerId = ~as.vector(data$Global_ID))

##UI

ui<-fluidPage(
  leafletOutput("map3")
)

## server

server<-function(input, output, session){

  output$map3 <- renderLeaflet({map3
  })

  logfilename<-"upstream"

  obs <-observe({
    c(input$map3_marker_click)
  })

  session$onSessionEnded(function() {
    obs$suspend()

    #    Also clean up the log file for this example
    unlink(logfilename)
  })

}

shinyApp(ui, server)

Shiny.bindAll(). Here is an example:

callback = JS("Shiny.unbindAll(table.table().node());
        Shiny.bindAll(table.table().node());")

server.R

      info <- eventReactive(input$choice, {
        inFile <- input$file
        if (is.null(inFile))
          return(NULL)
        isolate(f<-read.table(inFile$datapath, header = T,
                               sep = "\t"))
        f
      })
      output$table_display<-renderTable({
        f<-info()
        f<-subset(f, select=input$columns) #subsetting takes place here
        head(f)
      })
    }

messages.body_plain:
Hi, All,

I was able to create a carouselBox() function, along with carouselSets() and carouselItem() function, for showing a carousel in shinydashboard.

I want to further binding the id attribute in carouselSets, and using input$[id] on server side for referencing the active carouselItem. In my mind, this would ideally be a replication design on how tabsetPanel and tabPanel work with each other.

Here is a reproducible code to show what I want to achieve:

In app.r:

library(shiny)
library(shinydashboard)

source("carouselBox.r")

runApp(

  list(

    ui = shinyUI(

      dashboardPage(

        dashboardHeader(

          title = "Carousel Example"

        ),

        dashboardSidebar(

          sidebarMenu(

            id = "sidebar_main",

            # tags$li(class="header", "MAIN NAVIGATION"),

        ),

        dashboardBody(

          tabItems(

            tabItem(

              tabName = "TabsetPanelTab",

                id = "tabExample",

                ),

                tabPanel(

                  title = "Tab B", h4("This is TabPanel B")

                )

              ),

              box(

                title = "Which tabPanel is Active?",

                textOutput(outputId = "tabPanelActive")

              )

            ),

            tabItem(

              tabName = "CarouselTab",

              carouselBox(

                title = "Carousel Box", footer = NULL, status = "success",
                solidHeader = TRUE, background = NULL, width = 12L, # height = 400L,
                collapsible = TRUE, collapsed = FALSE,

                carouselSets(

                  id = "carouselExample",

                  carouselItem(

                    tags$img(src="http://placehold.it/900x500/39CCCC/ffffff&text=I+Love+Bootstrap"),

                    caption = "First Slide"

                  ),

                  carouselItem(

                    tags$img(src="http://placehold.it/900x500/3c8dbc/ffffff&text=I+Love+Bootstrap"),

                    caption = "Second Slide"

                  ),

                  carouselItem(

                    tags$img(src="http://placehold.it/900x500/f39c12/ffffff&text=I+Love+Bootstrap"),

                    caption = "Third Slide"

                  )

                )

              ),

              box(

                title = "Which CarouselItem is Active?",

                textOutput(outputId = "carouselActiveItem")

              )

            )

          )

        )

      )
    ),

    server = shinyServer(

      function(input, output, session) {

        output$tabPanelActive <- renderText({ paste0("Active TabPanel is <", input$tabExample, ">") })

        output$carouselActiveItem <- renderText({ paste0("Image would show only when open in Browser - not in Rstudio App. I want to know which one is active from input$carouselExample. How to binding the `id` attributes in carouselSets with carouselItem, something like binding tabsetPanel id with tabPanel? Thanks a lot!\n\n The current input$carouselExample would give: <", input$carouselExample, "> ...\n")})

      }

    )
  )
)

In carouselBox.r:

#' Create a carousel box for the main body of a dashboard.
#'
#' A \code{carouseleBox} displays \code{carouselSets} and \code{carouselItem} as
#' main box content, often structures as an \code{carouselSets} follows several
#' \code{carouselItem}s.
#'
#' @inheritParams box
#' @param ... For carousel items, this may consist of \code{\link{carouselSets}}s,
#'   which in turn includes one or more \code{\link{carouselItem}}s.
#' @param .list An optional list containing items to put in the carousel same as
#'   the \code{...} arguments, but in list format. This can be useful when working
#'   with programmatically generated items.
#'
#' @family boxes
#' @seealso \code{\link{box}} for usage examples.
#'
#' @rdname carouselBox
#' @export
carouselBox <- box

#' @rdname carouselBox
#' @export
carouselSets <- function(..., id = NULL, class = NULL, itemStartWith = 1L, .list = NULL) {

  if (is.null(id)) id <- paste0("carousel-generic", "-", sample(1000L, 1L))

  items <- c(list(...), .list)

  n <- max(1L, length(items))

  if (itemStartWith > n) itemStartWith <- 1L

  if ( n == 1L ) {

    items[["attribs"]][["class"]] <- paste0(items[["attribs"]][["class"]], " active")

  } else {

    items[[itemStartWith]][["attribs"]][["class"]] <- paste0(items[[itemStartWith]][["attribs"]][["class"]], " active")

  }

  tags$div(

    id = id,

    class = "carousel slide",

    class = if (!is.null(class)) class,

    `data-ride`="carousel",

    eval(parse(text = paste0(
      'tags$ol(',
      'class = "nav carousel-indicators shiny-carousel-input shiny-bound-input",',
      paste0(
        'tags$li(',
        '`data-target`=paste0("#", id), `data-slide-to`="', c(1L:n) - 1L, '", ',
        'class="', ifelse(c(1L:n) == itemStartWith, "active", ""), '"',
        ')',
        collapse = ", "
      ),
      ")"
    ))),

    tags$div(

      class = "carousel-inner",

      items

    ),

    tags$a(

      class = "left carousel-control",

      href = paste0("#", id),

      `data-slide` = "prev",

      tags$span(

        class = "fa fa-angle-left"

      )

    ),

    tags$a(

      class = "right carousel-control",

      href = paste0("#", id),

      `data-slide` = "next",

      tags$span(

        class = "fa fa-angle-right"

      )

    )

  )

}

#' @rdname carouselBox
#' @export
carouselItem <- function(..., caption = NULL, .list = NULL) {

  items <- c(list(...), .list)

  tags$div(

    class = "item",

    items,

    if (!is.null(caption)) tags$div(class = "carousel-caption", caption)

  )

}

I tried to follow the code in input_binding_tabinput.js in shiny source code, but lost.

I appreciate if anyone could guide me on how to make the binding work.

BTW, would anyone explain why shiny package put some javascript file in folder srcjs, and other javascript file in inst/www/shared?

Thank you very much.

Best Regards,
Guang Yang

messages.body_plain:
Of course. I was just using month.abb as an example (same thing for
LETTERS[1:5]). You can use any row names you want.

library(shiny)
library(DT)
shinyApp(
    ui = fluidPage(
        title = 'Radio buttons in a table',
        DT::dataTableOutput('foo'),
        verbatimTextOutput('sel')
    ),
    server = function(input, output, session) {

      mynames = month.abb
      mynames[1] = '1st'

      m = matrix(
            as.character(1:5), nrow = 12, ncol = 5, byrow = TRUE,

            dimnames = list(mynames, LETTERS[1:5])

        )
        for (i in seq_len(nrow(m))) {
            m[i, ] = sprintf(
                '<input type="radio" name="%s" value="%s"/>',

               mynames[i], m[i, ]
            )
        }

        m
        output$foo = DT::renderDataTable(
            m, escape = FALSE, selection = 'none', server = FALSE,
            options = list(dom = 't', paging = FALSE, ordering = FALSE),
            callback = JS("table.rows().every(function(i, tab, row) {
                          var $this = $(this.node());
                          $this.attr('id', this.data()[0]);
                          $this.addClass('shiny-input-radiogroup');
    });
                          Shiny.unbindAll(table.table().node());
                          Shiny.bindAll(table.table().node());")
        )
        output$sel = renderPrint({

            str(sapply(mynames, function(i) input[[i]]))
        })
        }
)

Regards,
Yihui

Good question. One way you can go is to add the IDs to a certain
column of the data, and hide this column, e.g. add the IDs to the
first column and hide it via the options

options = list(
  columnDefs = list(
    list(targets = 1, visible = FALSE)
  )
)

Full reference: https://datatables.net/reference/option/columnDefs

Then $this.attr('id', this.data()[1]);

I'm struggling with how to pass an input switch to dplyr's group_by_ in the code below.

I bolded the two parts of relevant code in the not-so-MRE below (ie, lines 9:11, and 24).

effectively, if the user selects "daily" in the UI, the resultant grouping should be group_by(year = year(my_date), month = month(my_date), day = day(my_date) in line 24, or remove ANY grouping as the data is already daily.

selecting "monthly", should yield group_by(year = year(my_date), month = month(my_date))

"yearly", should yield group_by(year = year(my_date))

I welcome meta-suggestions/ criticism about how my code/ structures are organized.

Thank you

library(shiny)
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)

ui <- fluidPage(
  dateInput("start", label = "start date", value = "2010-01-01"),
  dateInput("end", label = "end date", value = "2020-01-01"),
  selectInput("grouping_freq", label = "Granularity",
              choices = list("daily" = 1,"monthly" = 2, "Yearly" = 3),
              selected = 2),
  tableOutput("my_table")
)

server <- function(input, output) {

  df <- reactive({ data_frame(my_date = seq(input$start, input$end, by = 'day')) }) ## 10 years of daily data

  df2 <- reactive({ df() %>% mutate(dummy_data = cumsum(rnorm( nrow( df() ) ))) })

  output$my_table <- renderTable({
    df2() %>% group_by(year = year(my_date), month = month(my_date)) %>%
      summarise(dummy_data = sum(dummy_data), my_date = as.Date(min(my_date)))
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

Cross-post from stackoverflow here : http://stackoverflow.com/questions/38938894/blinking-ggplot-in-shiny-r-app

Question:

I'm doing a small shiny app that only has one ggplot that is updated every couple of seconds. It works, but the blinking is a bit annoying. I wonder if anyone has an idea about how to smooth it out. Example:

library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)

server <- shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {

    output$showplot <- renderPlot({
        grid <- expand.grid(1:3,1:3)
        nums <- rbinom(9,1,0.5)
        g <- ggplot(grid,aes(Var1,Var2)) +
            geom_tile(aes(fill = nums),colour="black") +
            guides(fill = FALSE) +
            theme(axis.title.x=element_blank(), axis.text.x=element_blank(), axis.ticks.x=element_blank()) +
            theme(axis.title.y=element_blank(), axis.text.y=element_blank(), axis.ticks.y=element_blank()) +
            theme(aspect.ratio=1)

        print(g)

        invalidateLater(1000,session)
   })

})

ui <- shinyUI(fluidPage(

    sidebarLayout(
        sidebarPanel(

        ),

    mainPanel(
        h5("Plot blinking"),
        plotOutput("showplot")
    )
)
))

runApp(list(ui = ui, server = server))

I should add that while looking around for a similar question, the solution provided was adding

tags$style(type="text/css",
    ".recalculating {opacity: 1.0;}" ),

as the first item in FluidPage. This doesn't seem to work for my case.

Any ideas? I though maybe I could somehow keep adding geom_tile layers instead of building a new plot everytime. Seems kind of a silly idea as it would grow forever though.

messages.subject: Re: Dynamically creating UI elements in a tree data structure
messages.subject_clean: Dynamically creating UI elements in a tree data structure
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I would use a global variable. Note the use of "<<-" to assign a "value" to the global variable.

sliceBox.tree <- list()

server <- function(input, output) {

  ...

  rootNode <- newNode(1, 0)

  sliceBox.tree <<- list(rootNode) # We'll store our nodes as a 1D list, so parent and child ID's are recorded as their indices in the list

  ...

  # Event handlers: specific function for particular button will run when that button is pressed

  observeEvent(v$counter, {
    for (id in 1:v$counter) {
      buttonID <- paste0("sliceBoxButton", id)
      observeEvent(input[[buttonID]], {
        v$counter <- v$counter + 1L
        print(paste0("Pressed ", buttonID))

        # Make a copy of slicebox
        sbt <- sliceBox.tree

        # Append new child to list of children

        numChildren <- length(sbt[[id]]$children)
        sbt[[id]]$children[v$counter] <- v$counter

        sbt[[v$counter]] <- newNode(v$counter, id)

        print(paste0("Appending node to tree at index ", v$counter))

        # assign the modified copy to the global slicebox
        sliceBox.tree <<- sbt
        print(sliceBox.tree)
      })
    }
  })

  ...

}

Best Sigbert

messages.body_plain:
Hi Daniel,

You can search if the header name exists before you try accessing your matrix with the given header name

For example:
testMatrix <- matrix(seq(1,10), nrow=2, ncol=5)
colnames(testMatrix) <- letters[1:5]

lookingFor <- "z"

# Check if the given name is a header name
if (lookingFor %in% colnames(testMatrix)) {
  ### Found it
  paste(lookingFor, " was found", sep="")
} else {
  ### Not Found
  paste(lookingFor, " was not found", sep="")
  #### can use stop() function to end function execution and return custom message
  # stop(paste(lookingFor, " was not found", sep=""))
}

Parth, the last one should've worked. Can you zip up that folder and send it to me so I can reproduce?

Dean, Barry, this may be misguided but I left global.R support out of shinyAppFile/shinyAppDir because I thought it was a bad idea to have multiple, relatively independent Shiny apps that run concurrently, to all make changes to the global environment. Especially since the single-file app.R style lets you declare variables that are accessible in both ui and server, but do not pollute the global environment.

Clearly it's a surprising behavior though. What do you think of the following alternatives:

1) Run global.R, let it modify the global environment, don't worry about collisions between different subapps
2) Run global.R but not in the global environment, just in an environment that ui.R and server.R (or app.R) inherit. I like the semantics but don't like that it's titled "global.R" and isn't global.
3) Don't run global.R, but if one is detected, emit a warning that it will be ignored

I probably just don't understand how global.R works. I always just assumed that it's a file that gets automatically "sourced" by both ui and server before the app starts, and that's it. messages.body_plain:
Just to be clear, it's not Shiny Server running multiple apps that's the problem--generally, all those different apps each run in their own process (or processes). Yikes, it would be total chaos otherwise.

It's the fact that you can compose multiple apps into a single app using shinyAppDir and shinyAppFile (by incorporating them into the UI of an app, or embedding them from inside a Shiny Rmd document <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com/authoring_embedded_shiny.html>), where there can potentially be a problem, because then those sub-apps all do run in the same process.

messages.body_plain: Hi there... since this post is very related to my problem, I wonder if someone could help? I have just started this thread . Thanks! On Thursday, December 3, 2015 at 9:07:29 AM UTC, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote: > Sorry I didn't have a chance to follow up--glad you were able to figure it out! > > On Wed, Dec 2, 2015 at 11:03 PM Bryan Britten wrote: > > So I figured out the answer. Modern web browsers don't allow for a cross between http://localhost and file:/// when referencing files. Since Shiny runs on http://localhost, the use of file:/// was throwing everything off. In addition, when an iframe attempts to load a file, such as a PDF, the directory in which the html files that served as the source for the iframe is saved is the working directory. So the filepath for the PDF needs to account for that, either by having the file in the same folder, or using "../some.pdf" notation. Lastly, file names cannot have spaces in them. This was the biggest thing causing my file to not be found. > > > > In the end, the two fixes were this: 1) make sure the HTML files I generate dynamically for the iframes and any files I want to embed are saved in the same directory, and 2) standardize the file names. > > > > On Tuesday, December 1, 2015 at 3:41:45 PM UTC-5, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote: > > > So you're saying that users will run these Shiny apps on their own computers (i.e. running R on their own machines)? messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Thanks for your bug report. Tried to understand the problem for some hours, and now that I found, I can't think of a way to fix it :
Drawn features are exported to R in GeoJSON format. GeoJSON doesn't handle the circle geometry, and circles are then stored as points with a radius attribute (outside the geometry).
When the coordinates change, the point change and is thus updated in R.
But when the radius changes, it's only an attribute of the json, not on the geojson, and thus, it"s not updated.

Right now, I can't think of any way to fix this behaviour, appart making some special rules for circles.
I will work on this in a few weeks, can't find the time before.

Sorry for this unresolved (at the time) issue :(

Regards,

Robin

> > #' @param x The dataframe returned from a shiny::fileInput
> > fixUploadedFilesNames <- function(x) {

> >    return()
> >  }
> >
> >  oldNames = x$datapath
> >  newNames = file.path(dirname(x$datapath),
> >                       x$name)
> >  file.rename(from = oldNames, to = newNames)
> >  x$datapath <- newNames
> >  x
> > }

messages.body_plain:
Thanks for your patience, Parth.

If you're publishing to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, the current method you're doing is correct (shinyAppFile("app.R"), without calling setwd first) but can you rename app.R to something else--like subapp.R? (And make the corresponding change to the shinyAppFile call as well, of course--e.g. shinyAppFile("subapp.R")) Oh, and you may also want to rename your Rmd file to index.Rmd, though I'm not 100% sure that's necessary.

I think what's happening is that the presence of app.R makes shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> treat the whole directory/project as a Shiny app with app.R at the top, rather than an Rmd document.

  sidebarPanel(
    sliderInput("obs", "Number of observations:",
                min = 0, max = 1000,  value = 500),
    actionButton("savePlot", "savePlot")
  ),
  mainPanel(
    # Use imageOutput to place the image on the page
    imageOutput("plot"),
    imageOutput("plot_as_svg")
  )
))

server.R
require("ggplot2")
library(svglite)

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {

  ## create plot with renderPlot()

      output$plot<- renderPlot({
        hist(rnorm(input$obs), main="Generated in renderPlot()")
        })

  ## create .svg file of the plot and render it with renderImage()

In my shiny app, data is updated daily, and so are some global variables my app needs to function correctly. Therefore, every time the underlying data updates I overwrite a file called "stage_data.Rdata" that contains the workspace needed by both my ui.R and server.R programs.

Here is the contents of global.R:

# clear workspace and load in new workspace just in case its changed
rm(list=ls())
load("stage_data.Rdata")

The problem: if global.R is not changed and re-saved, shiny server doesn't seem to re-run global.R and thus, my statement: load(stage_data.Rdata) doesn't run either. As a result, I'm working with old workspace variables until I intervene. Specifically, I open global.R and make some small change (like adding a space or #) and re-saving the program. If I restart shiny server, that also works. How can I make shiny server read global.R every session without my intervention?

messages.subject: Inconsistency with selectInput when choices=NULL in regards of multiple parameter
messages.subject_clean: Inconsistency with selectInput when choices=NULL in regards of multiple parameter
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

I have two selectInput. One with multiple = TRUE and one with multiple = FALSE. Both of them have the choices parameter equals to NULL.
With the one input with multiple=TRUE, the input value is NULL.
With the other one, it forces it to "".

I have been in the code under it and it seems that in that case shiny:::selectizeIt will always put the argument nonempty to TRUE and so the value will be forced to "".
Is there a way to force having a NULL value ?

Here is a code to demonstrate this issue :

library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  column(6,
         selectInput(inputId = "input1",
                     label = "input1",
                     choices = NULL,
                     selected = NULL,
                     multiple = FALSE
                     ),
         verbatimTextOutput("output1")
  ),
  column(6,
         selectInput(inputId = "input2",
                     label = "input2",
                     choices = NULL,
                     selected = NULL,
                     multiple = TRUE
                     ),
         verbatimTextOutput("output2")
  )
)

server <- shinyServer(function(input, output, session){
  output$output1 <- renderPrint(
    list(choices = input$input1,
         is.null = is.null(input$input1),
         length = length(input$input1))
  )
  output$output2 <- renderPrint(
    list(choices = input$input2,
         is.null = is.null(input$input2),
         length = length(input$input2))
  )
})

shinyApp(ui, server)

Thanks

messages.subject: Re: How to make an uploaded data reactive ?
messages.subject_clean: How to make an uploaded data reactive ?
messages.body_plain:
You need to extract the data you want to use into a reactive expression. Like userdata, below:

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  userdata <- reactive({

    inFile <- input$file1

    if (is.null(inFile))
      return(NULL)

    read.csv(inFile$datapath, header=input$header, sep=input$sep, quote=input$quote)
  })

  output$contents <- renderTable({
    userdata()
  })

  output$view <- renderTable({
    summary(userdata())  # or whatever
  })
})

You may want to watch the two parts of the Effective Reactive Programming tutorial here: https://www.rstudio.com/resources/webinars/shiny-developer-conference/

How should a ggolot2 visualization display a default condition in a shiny app?

For example, user interaction results in an empty data frame as input to ggplot2, yielding blank screen and error messages like these:

Error: Aesthetics must be either length 1 or the same as the data (1): y, x, fontface, size, fill, alpha, label
... and ...
Error: argument is of length zero

My solution is to test for the default condition and display a text box explanation instead of the ggplot2 viz.

Wondering of any suggestions for handling display of default ggplot2 conditions in shiny. Thanks

I had the same problem and I unfortunately haven't found a way to do it directly with a shiny option but you can use this piece of code (which works perfectly well for my shnyashboard app) :

tags$head(
   tags$meta(name = "viewport", content = "initial-scale=1, maximum-scale=1, user-scalable=no, width=device-width")
)

HTH ! :)

Best regards,

-- Aline

messages.body_plain: Hi All, Trying to speed up a Shiny app I found that, too my surprise, the speed issues were caused by the simple HTML functions such as "em" "strong" and "br". The following code illustrates this problem: > timer(for(i in 1:100000) j=i) # Just test how long the looping takes. Time difference of 0.03906202 secs > timer(for(i in 1:100000) s = paste0("","test","")) # Create a simple tag Time difference of 0.457031 secs > timer(for(i in 1:100000) s = em("test")) # Use the shiny function "em" Time difference of 4.987287 secs # 10 times slower. > This might not seem like an issue but when you are building a large table of HTML formatted values it can (and did) cause significant delays. David

messages.body_plain:
Sorry, there isn't currently a way to change this, but it's something we're considering for a future release.

One way around this is to limit the number of tables you show in each section/tab. Shiny will hold off on displaying data that isn't currently visible.

On Tue, Aug 30, 2016 at 10:06 AM Romeole Smiles <romeol...@gmail.com> wrote:

> I created a dashboard with 15 data tables in Shiny. Each table draws data from an API and this process takes some time. So I want to output each table to ui at a time such that users can read the first table while the other ones load. But it seems Shiny always holds all output until server function finishes execution. Is there a way to change this?
>

messages.subject: Re: Different Ui file for Mobile
messages.subject_clean: Different Ui file for Mobile
messages.body_plain:
This is a big topic, but the two main ways in traditional development are 1) conditional CSS using media queries, and 2) user agent sniffing.

#1 is how bootstrap (and flexdashboard) do this, it involves writing CSS rules that modify the styles of different elements depending on the size of the screen being used.

#2 is more antiquated and harder to maintain but ultimately more flexible, as you can send completely different HTML to each class of device. In Shiny it would look something like this:

ui <- function(request) {
  if (!is.null(request$HTTP_USER_AGENT) && grepl("\\bMobile\\b", request$HTTP_USER_AGENT)) {
    # mobile UI goes here
  } else {
    # desktop UI goes here
  }
}

I guess there's a third option--use fluidPage, fluidRow, and column intelligently (see the guide <http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/layout-guide.html>), and let bootstrap's responsive features <http://getbootstrap.com/css/> be enough.
